body:
Emily (SE): FYI — customer wants an air-gapped POC in their secure sandbox next week. Two big asks: extended offline bundle retention (90d) and ability to apply delta patches via USB. Need ops + commercial input.
Raj (Sales): Which customer? any leverage on budget?
Emily (SE): Gov contractor, SOC2-like requirements, pilot budget limited. They specifically asked for price for 90d vs our standard 30d retention and signed artifact guarantees.
Julie (Sales Lead): We usually treat extended retention as an add-on. I need a ballpark uplift and any operational blockers. Marco, can you estimate ops delta?
Marco (Ops): Technical constraints: 90d retention increases storage footprint and number of signed artifacts to host. For airgap, we support delta bundles but they must be precomputed and individually signed. For USB/sneakernet deliveries we require a signed manifest + per-chunk checksums.
Marco (Ops): Example verify flow we recommend to customers:
```
sha256sum redwood-bundle-v1.tar.gz
cosign verify --key /opt/keys/pub.pem redwood-bundle-v1.sig
```
Marco (Ops): Operationally we prefer default 30d to limit surface; 90d is fine but requires extra storage and retention SLAs. Quick ops delta: estimate +$0.20/GB/month for retention/replication and +40h engineering for delta prep and automation for the POC (one-time).
Raj (Sales): How do we handle licensing metering offline? They won't allow telemetry.
Marco (Ops): We can support offline metering via signed usage reports that the customer returns monthly. Enforcement is via bootstrap token TTL and signed attestations. We need legal to confirm audit rights language.
Emily (SE): Security questionnaire snippets — Q12: 'Who signs artifacts and how keys are protected?' Q17: 'Patch cadence and emergency hotfix path for air-gapped nodes'.
Marco (Ops): Q12 short answer: artifacts are signed with RSA/ECDSA keys stored in HSM. Customer can supply their own key or opt for Redwood-managed HSM. Verification is via cosign/sha256 as noted. Q17 short answer: standard cadence is monthly delta windows; emergency hotfix via signed hotfix bundle and manual push with documented rollback. SLA upgrade path available for enterprise customers.
Julie (Sales Lead): For SOW we should include: retention SLA, patch cadence (monthly + emergency), cost uplift, bundle verification acceptance criteria, and optional key escrow/escrowed signing. Also add a one-time engineering fee for USB/delivery prep.
ops-bot: Ticket CS-4521 created for 'airgap retention pricing quote' — assignee: Marco
Raj (Sales): Proposed pricing approach: base POC fee + retention add-on (15% uplift) + one-time delivery/engineering fee. We'll refine numbers after Marco's final ops estimate.
Emily (SE): Need to get the security questionnaire back to them by EOD Thursday. Marco — can you draft the Q12/Q17 boilerplate we can paste?
Marco (Ops): Drafting now. Short boilerplate (I'll also attach to CS-4521):
```
Q12: Artifacts signing: Redwood signs every release using keys stored in HSM or using customer-supplied keys. Verification is supported via cosign and SHA-256 checksums. Key custody options: Redwood-managed HSM, customer-managed HSM, or offline key exchange during POC.
Q17: Patch cadence: Regular monthly delta windows and documented patch notes. Hotfix path: emergency signed hotfix bundle with rollback instructions and manual approval. Expedited SLAs available under dedicated support contract.
```
Marco (Ops): Also note we output full bundles + delta set + signed manifest (SHA256 + signature) for each bundle. That should address their verification controls.
Julie (Sales Lead): LGTM. Raj, I want to sync on margins before I send commercial terms.
Raj (Sales): 30min after stand works. I'll sketch the margin and add the 40h eng fee.
Emily (SE): Customer also requested ability to pin to a specific model version and guarantee max upgrade frequency per month. Please confirm.
Marco (Ops): We support per-customer version pinning and manual rollouts. Recommend we include a 'pin-to-version' clause in the SOW and a limit on automatic rollouts (e.g., max 1 non-security upgrade/month unless opt-in).
Emily (SE): Thank you — once the draft answers are in CS-4521 I'll paste into the questionnaire. :+1:
Marco (Ops): Draft posted to CS-4521. Also documenting token TTL approach for offline license enforcement and the optional escrow model.
Emily (SE): Closing loop — customer deadline is EOD Thu. I'll follow up if they need fingerprints or sample manifests.
Julie (Sales Lead): Thanks all.
